purpose: Read-only quality audit rules for existing and candidate card JSON. This audit surfaces mechanical blockers and content-risk signals; it is not formal release approval.

pre_cutover_report_archive.active_repository_immutability_proof: The index bytes and every referenced legacy review-record byte sequence must equal their versions in the active repository commit that introduced the index. source_commit identifies the archived pre-cutover history and is not assumed to resolve inside the cut-over active Git history.

legacy_scoped_report_archive.scope: immutable historical diagnostic artifacts created before current scoped-report ok and rule-completeness semantics
legacy_scoped_report_archive.mutation_policy: forbidden; every listed path and hash must resolve identically at the active repository index-introduction commit, and new evidence must use a new direct scoped-report path and current audit replay

severity_levels.meaning: A mechanical card-shape issue that blocks candidate or formal batch scope until fixed.
A likely content-quality problem that requires semantic model review before current authorization.
Missing review evidence or quality metadata that prevents formal use claims.
Source provenance or generation status that must stay visible during review.

rules.description: A multiple-choice card must expose at least two options.
A multiple-choice answer should match one of the visible option keys or option texts.

A multiple-choice front-side prompt, including preview-rendered task_schema guide fields, must not name the correct option text, distinctive long-option answer phrases in answer-summary guide text, distinctive correct-option phrases inside visible guide/success criteria, answer-summary guide tokens, short preposition answer text, answer-example text, answer semantic gloss such as probability, evidence strength, practicality, research variable-control meaning, or preposition semantic-role meaning outside the visible option list, candidate pool, source/context material, or a topic label that lists multiple answer candidates. It also must not use answer-hindsight guide language that tells the learner the correct answer/option, labels a structural side as the answer candidate, identifies which side is the true cause/result/main point/condition, or asks which option all answer clues hit.

A front-side prompt, including preview-rendered task_schema guide fields, must not tell the learner that a specific clue is the key, the key to solving the question, or the key to cracking or locking the answer. That belongs on the analysis side after the learner has attempted the card.
The front side is missing or too short to stand as an independent learning task.
The back-side explanation is missing or too short to support mechanism, transfer, and error handling.
The front side matches broad template-like prompts that may not carry box-specific learning value.
The analysis matches repeated generic explanation patterns instead of card-specific reasoning.
The same normalized front text appears on multiple cards.
The same normalized analysis text appears on multiple cards.
The card has no quality_metadata block, so it cannot pass the sample quality workflow.
The source_ref provenance_status is unverified or missing.
The source_ref.type or quality_metadata.material.text_source_type is AI-generated, simulated, or synthetic and must not be labeled as true exam content.

report_contract.card_issue_index_role: Per-card counts by severity and rule. Review records must use this index to store a scoped summary for their own card_ids instead of relying only on corpus-level totals.

scoped_report_contract.purpose: Per-sample audit evidence that can be committed with a content sample PR without refreshing global reports.
scoped_report_contract.ok_semantics: A scoped report is ok only when all requested card_ids exist and scoped_hard_blocker_issues is empty.
scoped_report_contract.tracked_artifact_validation: Every changed or newly added scoped report must exactly match a current immutable-HEAD audit replay for its declared card IDs. Standalone harness validation recursively rejects malformed artifacts; current-fingerprint artifacts are replayed against the current global audit, while structurally valid unchanged historical artifacts may retain their historical fingerprint. An unchanged historical self-review bound to such an artifact validates against that artifact's immutable fingerprint and recorded rule set without current-card or current-track parity; changing the review requires a direct current replay. An unchanged historical approval remains archive evidence. Current-authorization consumers require approval, linked self-review, both scoped reports, scripts/audit_card_quality.mjs, and spec/card-quality-audit.json to be regular committed evidence or authority whose worktree, index, and one fixed HEAD modes and bytes agree. They independently regenerate the complete current audit, exactly replay both scoped reports, and recheck the fixed HEAD/index snapshot, captured file bytes/modes, and corpus fingerprint before returning. Merely being tracked, matching only the corpus digest, using a self-declared summary, or claiming zero blockers is insufficient. Explicit legacy exceptions are limited to the hash-pinned legacy_scoped_report_archive.

report_freshness_policy.candidate_scoped_evidence_exception: On candidate content PRs, a stale global report may be tolerated only when a current scoped audit report exists for the changed card corpus and validate_pr_scope blocks global report refreshes plus non-scope self-review churn.
